name: Italian Grand Prix
sources_2026_10_03: Race-story notes added from Formula1.com, FIA, BBC Sport, Sky Sports, Pit Debrief, PlanetF1 and Autosport, all 2026-09-06 to 2026-09-07; official FIA final classification used for results and penalties. Verified 2026-10-03 against the FIA final classification, final starting grid and qualifying classification: Lawson and Alonso pit-lane starts; per-driver fastLap backfilled from the formula1.com fastest-laps table (Leclerc set no representative lap).
summary: Kimi Antonelli charged from P19 after a 30-place power-unit penalty to win his home Italian Grand Prix, passing George Russell with three laps left for a 3.857s victory. Charles Leclerc's heavy Parabolica crash on lap two caused the red flag; after the restart, Gasly's shock pole faded to seventh as Antonelli recovered through the field. A VSC for Lance Stroll's hydraulics failure let Antonelli pit for fresh tyres while Russell stayed out, setting up the late Mercedes fight; Verstappen completed the podium and Norris passed Piastri for fourth. Three cars retired (Leclerc, Stroll and Alonso), and Sergio Perez received a five-second penalty for failing to follow Race Director instructions; Audi lodged an appeal over the stewards' ruling on Tsunoda's extra formation lap.

classification.stewardNote: Race time 1:51:15.281. Started P19 after a 30-place grid penalty for additional power unit elements; recovered from the back of the grid to win, becoming the first Italian winner of the Italian GP since 1966. Set the race's fastest lap on the final lap. Extends championship lead over Russell to 66 points.
+3.857s. Started P2, 0.060s off Gasly's pole time; led for much of the race before Antonelli's late move.
+14.718s. Recovered from P5 on the grid; held off both McLarens to the flag.
+19.056s. Passed team mate Piastri on the final lap at Ascari for P4.
